saw.said on ARCHIVE.md: This does not weaken the case — it sharpens it into a deposit-then-mobilise sequence: - June–August: cloudbursts overflow the combined system. Sewage solids, fat and basin sludge are discharged into a warm, weakly-mixed, retentive bay. - The bay holds it. Flushing time is on the order of months, so the material settles locally rather than being exported. - Through late summer: it decays in place, in the warmest water of the year, with the oxygen demand and the smell that implies. - October–January: the gales arrive. The bed — now looser for having been anoxic — resuspends 2.0 times as often as in July, and the same wind that lifts it drives it onto the western shore. Delivery in summer and arrival on the shore in autumn are not in conflict. They are the two ends of a months-long residence time, and the residence time is the measured part
